using System;

namespace Orleans.Clustering.Cosmos.Tests

    public class CosmosClusteringProviderBuilderTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public void Configure_SiloBuilder_UsesConnectionStringFromRootConfiguration_WhenConnectionNameProvidedAndConnectionStringEmpty()
        {
            // Arrange
            var builderMock = new Mock<ISiloBuilder>();
            var optionsBuilderMock = new Mock<ICosmosClusteringOptionsBuilder>();
            var optionsMock = new Mock<ICosmosClusteringOptions>();
            var serviceProviderMock = new Mock<IServiceProvider>();
            var configurationSectionMock = new Mock<IConfigurationSection>();
            var rootConfigurationMock = new Mock<IConfiguration>();

            // Setup configuration section keys
            configurationSectionMock.Setup(c => c["ServiceKey"]).Returns(string.Empty);
            configurationSectionMock.Setup(c => c["ConnectionName"]).Returns("MyConnectionName");
            configurationSectionMock.Setup(c => c["ConnectionString"]).Returns(string.Empty);

            // Setup root configuration to return a connection string for the connection name
            rootConfigurationMock.Setup(c => c.GetConnectionString("MyConnectionName")).Returns("FakeConnectionString");

            // Setup service provider to return root configuration
            serviceProviderMock.Setup(sp => sp.GetService(typeof(IConfiguration))).Returns(rootConfigurationMock.Object);

            // Setup options builder to call Configure with a callback that we can invoke
            optionsBuilderMock.Setup(ob => ob.Configure(It.IsAny<Action<ICosmosClusteringOptions, IServiceProvider>>()))
                .Callback<Action<ICosmosClusteringOptions, IServiceProvider>>(callback =>
                {
                    callback(optionsMock.Object, serviceProviderMock.Object);
                })
                .Returns(optionsBuilderMock.Object);

            // Setup builder to call UseCosmosClustering with the options builder
            builderMock.Setup(b => b.UseCosmosClustering(It.IsAny<Action<ICosmosClusteringOptionsBuilder>>()))
                .Callback<Action<ICosmosClusteringOptionsBuilder>>(configure =>
                {
                    configure(optionsBuilderMock.Object);
                })
                .Returns(builderMock.Object);

            var providerBuilder = new CosmosClusteringProviderBuilder();

            // Act
            providerBuilder.Configure(builderMock.Object, null, configurationSectionMock.Object);

            // Assert
            optionsMock.Verify(o => o.ConfigureCosmosClient("FakeConnectionString"), Times.Once);
        }

The class CosmosClusteringProviderBuilder is internal, so I cannot access it directly from the test project. Also, the builder methods expect concrete builder types (ISiloBuilder and IClientBuilder) and concrete options types, not the interfaces I tried to mock.

I will try to read the ISiloBuilder and IClientBuilder interfaces to understand how to mock or substitute them for testing. Then I can write tests that call Configure with mocks for the configuration and service provider to verify the call to GetConnectionString. I will start by reading the ISiloBuilder interface.

The ISiloBuilder and IClientBuilder interfaces require Services and Configuration properties that I must implement in the test mocks. I will add these properties to the test builder classes and use minimal implementations to satisfy the interface. Then I will resubmit the test. I will keep the rest of the test as is.
